rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi says Qur'anic أن لا is normally joined, but ten loci are written separately where the clause's certainty and necessity appear; this occurrence is among them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أن لا يدخلنها ﴾ فى القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He sees the emphatic prediction fulfilled: no poor person entered the orchard, though its owners' plan and expectation failed in how that happened.
rows.anchor: فلم يدخلها عليهم مسكين على غير ما قصدوا وتخيلوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article's assimilated lām is normally written because definiteness should clarify and expose the word; he explains concealment in semantically obscure forms through three kinds of darkness.
rows.anchor: وشأن المعرف أن يكون أبين وأظهر لا أخفى وأستر ظهرت فى الخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In two loci, al-Ayka is written as ليكة after hamza-vowel transfer, loss of hamzat al-waṣl and an alif; the compressed spelling condenses each story, with the Ṣād group called al-Aḥzāb.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الأيكة نقلت حركة همزتها على لام التعريف وسقطت همزة الوصل

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most grammarians allow calling Qur'anic wording زائد because this is familiar Arabic usage; such wording can provide emphasis or preparation, just as deletion can abbreviate.
rows.anchor: فذهب الأكثرون إلى جواز إطلاق الزائد فى القرآن نظرا إلى أنه نزل بلسان القوم

rows.speaker: منهم من لا يرى الزيادة
rows.claim: Other grammarians reject the label زائد altogether, arguing that each apparently extra expression has a particular purpose and meaning.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من لا يرى الزيادة فى شىء من الكلام ويقول هذه الألفاظ المحمولة على الزيادة جاءت لفوائد ومعان تخصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi resolves the dispute: if زائد meant wholly purposeless, it would be absurd; every word is needed, though its function may differ from that of other words.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أنه إن أريد بالزيادة إثبات معنى لا حاجة إليه فباطل لأنه عبث فتعين أن إلينا به حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scholars often call زائد a ṣila, while others call it muqḥam; either label appears in fluent expression.
rows.anchor: وكثير من القدماء يسمون الزائد صلة وبعضهم يسميه مقحما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects strained parsing that makes للفقراء a substitute for ولذي القربى, driven by the Hanafi rule that kinship alone gives no entitlement, or makes الذين ظلموا a substitute for للناس.
rows.anchor: الرابع تجنب الأعاريب التى هى خلاف الظاهر والمنافية لنظم الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoid remote ellipsis and complex metaphor; read اغفر لنا and اهدنا as supplication or request, not command, out of deference since command can imply superiority.
rows.anchor: فعلى دعاء أو سؤال ولا نقول فعلى أمر تأدبا من جهة أن الأمر يستلزم العلو

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: Al-Sirafi parses قائما بالقسط as a circumstantial accusative referring to God, while explaining that grammatical labels describe wording and cannot exhaust the inner truth of the meaning.
rows.anchor: بم انتصب قال بالحال قلت لمن الحال قال لله تعالى قلت فيقال لله حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is a matter of fear for believers, as shown by the statement that they are apprehensive of it; al-Zarkashi counts لعل الساعة قريب as an example of لعل used in fear.
rows.anchor: فان الساعة مخوفة في حق المؤمنين بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi rejects al-Zamakhshari's denial that this verse belongs to the category of لعل used for fear.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا رد على الزمخشرى حيث انكر إن تكون هذه الآية من هذا القبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine لعل retains its ordinary hopeful force: when a generous speaker uses it for a desired good, it implicitly promises that good, as in the call to worship for taqwa.
rows.anchor: من الكريم للمخاطبين في ذلك المحبوب تعريض بالوعد

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Malik and Abu Hanifa say that the divine law is binding, cited while explaining the inducement to reach the high rank of taqwa through faith.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم قال مالك وأبو حنيفة الشرع ملزم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God's inducement is certain like a promise; al-Zarkashi sees rational Mu'tazili obligation in this and says hope-inducing wording prevents complacency.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الزمخشرى وقد جاءت على سبيل الاطماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi argues that inducement without certainty is fitting, so people do not become complacent; he illustrates this with the call to repent and hope for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وهذا فيه رائحة الاعتزال فى الايجاب العقلى وانما يحسن الاطماع دون التحقيق كيلا يتكل العباد

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses لعل as hope and apprehension.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب لعل طمع واشفاق

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say لعل from God is obligatory and interpret it as لكي, since hope and apprehension cannot properly be attributed to God.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين إن لعل من الله واجبة وفسر في كثير من المواضع ب لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope or apprehension expressed by لعل can belong to the addressee or another party: the first example hopes Pharaoh will follow, and the second has Moses and Aaron hoping he will heed them.
rows.anchor: فذلك طمع منهم فى فرعون

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq uses the dual المربدان although al-Zarkashi says Basra had only one Mirbad; the text also cites الرقمتين and المكتين as place-name duals.
rows.anchor: وقول الفرزدق … عشية سال المربدان

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's الديرين is understood as Dair al-Walid, put in the dual by reference to the surrounding area.
rows.anchor: وقول جرير … لما مررت بالديرين

rows.speaker: ابن حزم والماوردي
rows.claim: Ibn Hazm and al-Mawardi take the pronoun in فإنه رجس back to the nearer الخنزير rather than لحم; some later scholars strengthen this by the rule that a pronoun refers to the modified noun.
rows.anchor: وعند التعارض راعى ابن حزم والماوردي الأصل الأول فقالا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority answer that nearest-antecedent agreement is not absolute; when principles conflict, outside evidence decides, and choosing the antecedent satisfying both is preferable, as al-Mawardi does for the pig containing the meat.
rows.anchor: وللجمهور أن يقولوا وكذا عوده للأقرب ليس بمطرد فقد يخرج عن الأصل لدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates that a pronoun can refer to the possessive's genitive complement, not the nearer possessed noun, with إياه referring to God in this example.
rows.anchor: فقد يعود إلى المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For adjective agreement, he cites سبع بقرات سمان as an example of the relevant rule concerning a following adjective.
rows.anchor: وكذا الصفة فإنها كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فظلت أعناقهم لها خاضعين, خاضعين agrees with the possessive's genitive complement; if it described أعناق, it would be خاضعة.
rows.anchor: فأخبر خاضعين عن المضاف إليه ولو أخبر عن المضاف لقال خاضعة

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The authoritative reading takes the pronoun in لأظنه to refer to Moses, not the added noun إله; Pharaoh's phrase corrects his earlier wording إله موسى.
rows.anchor: فقد عاد الضمير فى قول المحققين للمضاف غليه وهو موسى والظن بفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After أو, the default is a singular pronoun because it selects one of two; explanations of فالله أولى بهما are that أو means واو, the referents are two litigants, or it marks kinds rather than coordination.
rows.anchor: إذا عطف ب أو وجب إفراد الضمير نحو إن جاء زيد أو عمرو فأكرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, conjunction with واو normally calls for a dual pronoun; the verse والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه is an exception discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وعكس هذا إذا عطف بالواو وجب تثنية الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضحاها means the forenoon of that same day; al-Zarkashi says the short part stands for the whole.
rows.anchor: أي ضحى يومها فدل بالجزء على الكل

rows.speaker: عز الدين
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam says adding ضحى to the day of عشية makes the two spans comparable, preserving the contrast between a long and short stay; without it, a long-day forenoon could equal a short-day evening.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين وإنما أضاف الضحى إلى نهار العشية لأنه لو أطلقها من غير إضافة لم يحسن الترديد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says rhyme should be preserved only when meanings and structure remain sound; sounding ornament alone is not eloquence, and some word order serves exclusivity rather than rhyme.
rows.anchor: لا تحسن المحافظة على الفواصل لمجردها إلا مع بقاء المعانى على سدادها على النهج الذى يقتضيه حسن النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawasil may have identical or merely close final letters; either is praiseworthy when natural and meaning-led, while forced endings that distort meaning are blameworthy. The Qur'an uses the natural forms.
rows.anchor: فالقسم الأول هو المحمود الدال على الثقافة وحسن البيان والثانى هو المذموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is dropped from يسر to match the sūra's verse endings.
rows.anchor: وحذفت الياء من ﴿ يسر ﴾ طلبا للموافقة فى الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse-counting discussion notes choices to omit these two endings, while related endings are counted for rhyme or analogy, including لأولي الألباب, على الله كذبا, and والسلوى.
rows.anchor: وعلى ترك عد ﴿ أفغير دين الله يبغون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala is counted differently because it came as part of a verse in some readings; readers of those modes count it, while others omit it and count a replacement after اهدنا to keep al-Fatiha seven verses.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بحرف نزلت فيه عدها آية ولم يحتج إلى إثباتها بالقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing the divine hadith dividing prayer between God and the servant, he says المستقيم is settled and the verse boundary is arranged after اهدنا, with عليهم as the first ending matching the prior rhyme.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بينى وبين عبدى نصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening letters can be counted as verses because they stand independently and fit rhyme, or excluded because their lengths vary and they syntactically attach to what follows.
rows.anchor: ومنها حروف الفواتح فوجه عدها استقلالها على الرفع والنصب ومناسبة الروى والردف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Baqara, عذاب أليم and إنما نحن مصلحون may be counted for rhyme, or excluded because each is syntactically connected to what follows.
rows.anchor: ومنها بالبقرة ﴿ عذاب أليم ﴾ و ﴿ إنما نحن مصلحون ﴾ فوجه عده مناسبة الروى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending إلى بني إسرائيل in Aal Imran is counted by analogy with similar endings in al-A'raf, al-Shu'ara, and al-Sajda.
rows.anchor: ومنها ﴿ إلى بني إسرائيل ﴾ بآل عمران حملا على ما فى الأعراف والشعراء والسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فبشر عباد in al-Zumar is counted as an ending because what follows can be estimated as both an object and a predicate.
rows.anchor: ومنها ﴿ فبشر عباد ﴾ بالزمر لتقدير تاليه مفعولا ومبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one-word openings of al-Tur, al-Rahman, al-Haqqa, al-Qari'a, and al-Asr are counted by analogy with al-Fajr and al-Duha for rhyme, though their quantities differ.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والطور ﴾ و ﴿ الرحمن ﴾ و ﴿ الحاقة ﴾ و ﴿ القارعة ﴾ و ﴿ والعصر ﴾ حملا على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form يتذكر with tāʾ is listed in al-Ra'd, Ta-Ha, Fatir, Sad, al-Zumar, Ghafir, al-Nazi'at, and al-Fajr.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يتذكر ﴾ بتاء فى الرعد وطه والملائكة وص والزمر والمؤمن والنازعات والفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifteen sūras open with an oath, including al-Fajr and al-Asr; this is the fifth listed mode of sūra opening.
rows.anchor: الخامس القسم نحو ﴿ والصافات ﴾ ﴿ والذاريات ﴾ ﴿ والطور ﴾ ﴿ والنجم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven sūras instead open with a conditional, introduced as the sixth mode of sūra opening.
rows.anchor: السادس الشرط نحو ﴿ إذا وقعت الواقعة ﴾ ﴿ إذا جاءك المنافقون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported Meccan revelation order, al-Fajr comes ninth, after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
rows.anchor: ثم ﴿ والليل إذا يغشى ﴾ ثم ﴿ والفجر ﴾ ثم ﴿ والضحى ﴾

rows.speaker: حميد الأعرج
rows.claim: Humayd al-A'raj places the Quran's midpoint at the phrase معي صبرا in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: وقال حميد الأعرج نصفه ﴿ معي صبرا ﴾ فى الكهف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another midpoint location proposed is the letter ʿayn in تستطيع.
rows.anchor: وقيل عين ﴿ تستطيع ﴾ وقيل ثانى لامى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further proposal places the midpoint at the second lām of وليتلطف.
rows.anchor: وقيل ثانى لامى ﴿ وليتلطف ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse-count differences arise because the Prophet paused at verse endings by instruction, but sometimes continued to complete the sense, leading listeners to think a boundary was absent.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن سبب اختلاف العلماء فى عد الآى والكلم والحروف أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقف على رءوس الآى للتوقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala is counted in readings where it descended with the sūra and omitted in readings where it did not.
rows.anchor: وأيضا البسملة نزلت مع السورة فى بعض الأحرف السبعة فمن قرأ بحرف نزلت فيه عدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Word-count disagreements reflect the fact that a word can be assessed by its literal or figurative meaning, its written form, or convention; scholars choose among these valid measures.
rows.anchor: وسبب الاختلاف فى الكلمة أن الكلمة لها حقيقة ومجاز ورسم واعتبار كل منها جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara is the longest sūra and al-Kawthar the shortest.
rows.anchor: وأطول سورة فى القرآن هى البقرة وأقصرها الكوثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debt verse is longest at 128 words and 540 letters; al-Duha then al-Fajr are shortest. He rejects مدهامتان and ثم نظر as shorter candidates based on their letter or word counts.
rows.anchor: وأطول آية فيه آية الدين مائة وثمانية وعشرون كلمة وخمسمائة وأربعون حرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The longest unaugmented written and spoken word is فأسقيناكموه at eleven letters, followed by اقترفتموها at ten; ليستخلفنهم has nine spoken and ten estimated letters.
rows.anchor: وأطول كلمة فيه لفظا وكتابة بلا زيادة ﴿ فأسقيناكموه ﴾ أحد عشر لفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortest word includes the preposition ب, one letter rather than two, contrary to al-Dani's view.
rows.anchor: وأقصرها نحو باء الجر حرف واحد لا أنها حرفان خلافا للدانى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says verse boundaries are fixed by revelation, not analogy; Kufans count some fawātiḥ as verses, while other schools count none of them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى الآيات علم توقيف لا مجال للقياس فيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some explain counting يس but not طس by saying طس resembles a standalone proper name, whereas يس resembles a sentence because no single word begins with ياء.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إنما عدوا ﴿ يس ﴾ آية ولم يعدوا ﴿ طس ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi cites reports that al-Fatiha has seven verses and al-Mulk thirty, and that the Prophet recited Aal Imran's final ten; verse counts should follow early Muslims' practice.
rows.anchor: ذكر النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الفاتحة سبع آيات وسورة الملك ثلاثون آية وصح أنه قرأ العشر الآيات الخواتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word is a single utterance, potentially two to ten letters; al-Fajr, al-Duha, and al-Asr can each be a one-word verse, as can some opening letters for Kufans.
rows.anchor: وأما الكلمة فهى اللفظة الواحدة وقد تكون على حرفين مثل ما ولى وله ولك

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Abu Amr al-Dani says مدهامتان in al-Rahman is the only word that is itself a verse.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو الدانى لا أعلم كلمة هى وحدها آية إلا قوله ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾ فى سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Maki's first category allows stopping at كلا as denial of what precedes; this is preferred at eleven places, including al-Fajr, though restarting can make it an emphatic opening.
rows.anchor: وقسمها مكى أربعة أقسام الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maki's second category is syntactically tied to context, so one should not pause at كلا; beginning with it is preferable in these eighteen locations, including the Fajr passage.
rows.anchor: الثانى مالا يحسن الوقف عليه فيها ولا يكون الابتداء بها

rows.speaker: حازم
rows.claim: Hazim and others distinguish simile from metaphor: a simile permits restoring a comparison particle, while a metaphor does not; al-Rummani reads مبصرة as making its beholder see, not as a simile.
rows.anchor: كما قاله حازم وغيره أن الاستعارة وإن كان فيها معنى التشبيه فتقدير حرف التشبيه لا يجوز فيها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and other investigators call صم بكم عمي an emphatic simile because the hypocrites, its compared subject, are understood; a metaphor leaves that subject unstated.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلف البيانيون فى نحو قوله تعالى ﴿ صم بكم عمي ﴾ 1 إنه تشبيه بليغ أو استعارة والمحققون

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki says metaphor requires that the surface wording could bear a literal reading; زيد أسد cannot, so it cannot be metaphor under that condition.
rows.anchor: وقال السكاكى لأن من شرط الاستعارة إمكان حمل الكلام على الحقيقة فى الظاهر

words: الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thread phrase is a simile, not metaphor, because both terms are stated and من الفجر clarifies the white thread; without clarification it would be metaphor, but the image would not be inferable.
rows.anchor: فهذا تشبيه لا استعارة لذكر الطرفين الخيط الأسود وهو ما يمتد معه من غسق الليل شبيها بخيط أسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Asr is listed among thirty-one sūras containing both abrogating and abrogated material.
rows.anchor: والشورى والقتال والذاريات والطور والواقعة

words: لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم
rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi calls this a unique verse whose opening is abrogated and ending abrogates: enjoining right and forbidding wrong supersedes عليكم أنفسكم.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن العربى فى أحكامه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: The text-repealed, ruling-retained category is illustrated by the stoning wording once recited in al-Nur; Umar said he would have written it himself but feared people would accuse him of adding to scripture. Al-Bukhari transmits it in suspended form.
rows.anchor: كما روى أنه كان يقال فى سورة النور ( الشيخ والشيخة إذا زنيا فارجموهما ألبته نكالا من الله )
